verses.text: For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm by Asaph. A song. People know God in Judah. His name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem, and his home is in Zion.
That’s where he broke the flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.
You shine with glory, more majestic than mountains full of prey.
The bravest warriors lie stripped of what they had. They’ve fallen into their last sleep. None of them can lift a hand.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, horse and chariot alike fall still in the sleep of death.
You’re the one to fear. When you’re angry, who can stand before you?
You handed down your judgment from heaven. The earth trembled and went quiet
when you rose to judge, God, to save everyone on earth who was suffering. Selah.
Even human anger ends up bringing you praise. You hold back those who survive your wrath.
Make your vows to the LORD your God and keep them! Let everyone around him bring gifts to the one who fills them with awe.
He breaks the spirit of rulers. Even the kings of the earth fear him.
